title: Trigger CVE re-enrichment on service drift detection
description:
Legacy Daemon.compare_parameters re-invoked search_vulnerabilities() after product/version changes to keep vuln catalog fresh. Implement similar behavior for modern system.

## Legacy Behavior (daemon.py)
When service drift detected (product/version change):
1. Emit SERVICE_DRIFT notification
2. Immediately call search_vulnerabilities() with new product/version
3. Update vuln catalog with fresh CVE data

## Proposed Implementation

### Option A: Immediate Re-enrichment (aggressive)
- Trigger CVE enrichment job synchronously after SERVICE_DRIFT
- Ensures vuln data always matches current service fingerprint
- May cause API rate limit issues if many drifts occur

### Option B: Flag for Next Scheduled Enrichment (conservative)
- Mark device.needsEnrichment = true when SERVICE_DRIFT emitted
- Next scheduled enrichment picks up flagged devices first
- Less API load, acceptable staleness (next scan cycle)

### Option C: Hybrid (recommended)
- Immediate enrichment for CRITICAL/HIGH product changes (e.g., OpenSSH → unknown)
- Scheduled enrichment for INFO version bumps (e.g., nginx 1.18 → 1.19)

## Implementation Tasks
- [ ] Add enrichment trigger hook to SERVICE_DRIFT emission
- [ ] Create lightweight job queue for CVE re-enrichment
- [ ] Add device.needsEnrichment flag or similar tracking
- [ ] Handle Necto API rate limits gracefully
- [ ] Add telemetry for re-enrichment triggers

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Product changes trigger CVE enrichment within [TBD] timeframe
- [ ] API rate limits respected (no 429 errors)
- [ ] Enrichment results reflected in next notification cycle
- [ ] Telemetry tracks re-enrichment success/failure rates

## Context
- Current behavior: SERVICE_DRIFT notifications fire, but CVE data may be stale
- User impact: Drift to vulnerable product not flagged until next scheduled scan
- Related: sec-8sh (service drift detection), sec-v6e (metadata.lastChangedAt)

title: Expose per-port drift history timeline in UI/API
description:
Surface per-port service change timeline to make drift data actionable for users. Legacy system kept implicit audit via notifications; we can do better with structured portSnapshots.metadata.

## Current State
- portSnapshots.metadata has firstSeenAt/lastChangedAt/lastSeenAt timestamps
- SERVICE_DRIFT notifications emitted on changes
- No structured timeline of changes (users dig through notifications)

## Proposed Feature

### API Endpoint
GET /api/devices/{deviceId}/ports/{port}/history
Response:
```json
{
  "port": 80,
  "protocol": "tcp",
  "timeline": [
    {
      "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z",
      "event": "SERVICE_DRIFT",
      "changes": {
        "product": { "old": "nginx", "new": "apache" },
        "version": { "old": "1.18.0", "new": "2.4.0" }
      },
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "notificationId": "notif_123",
      "scanRunId": "scan_456"
    },
    {
      "timestamp": "2025-01-10T08:00:00Z",
      "event": "NEW_PORT",
      "service": { "product": "nginx", "version": "1.18.0" },
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "notificationId": "notif_100"
    }
  ]
}
```

### UI Component (Port Detail Modal)
- Timeline visualization (vertical timeline with icons)
- Expandable change details (old → new comparison)
- Link to notification for context
- Filter by event type (NEW_PORT, SERVICE_DRIFT, CLOSED_PORT)

### Data Source Options

**Option A: Query notifications table**
- Join notifications.data with scanRuns
- Filter by deviceId + port + type IN (NEW_PORT, CLOSED_PORT, SERVICE_DRIFT)
- Pro: Immediate, no schema changes
- Con: Missing drift events if notification suppressed/deduped

**Option B: Scan resultSummary diffing**
- Query all scanRuns for device, diff portSnapshots chronologically
- Pro: Complete history regardless of notifications
- Con: Expensive for devices with many scans

**Option C: Hybrid (recommended)**
- Store drift events in new port_history table
- Populated during change detection (alongside notifications)
- Indexed by (deviceId, port, protocol, timestamp)
- Pro: Fast queries, complete history, decoupled from notifications

## Implementation Tasks
- [ ] Design port_history schema (if Option C)
- [ ] Implement API endpoint for timeline retrieval
- [ ] Create UI component (timeline visualization)
- [ ] Add filtering/pagination for long histories
- [ ] Expose in port detail modal / asset detail page

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Users can view complete drift history for any port
- [ ] Timeline shows old → new values for each change
- [ ] Links to notifications and scan runs work
- [ ] UI handles ports with 100+ drift events gracefully

## Context

- User pain: "What changed on this port last month?" requires digging through notifications
- Related: sec-8sh (drift detection), sec-v6e (metadata.lastChangedAt)

title: Update DiscoveryStatus type definitions
Context-aware service drift severity - intelligent severity mapping based on service criticality
description:
Enhance service drift severity logic beyond flat priority 70 mapping by considering service criticality, known auto-updating services, and organizational context.

## Current Behavior
- All product changes = MEDIUM severity
- All version changes = INFO severity
- No consideration of service criticality or update patterns

## Proposed Enhancements

### 1. Critical Service Detection
Raise severity for drift on high-value targets:
- Authentication gateways (OAuth, SAML, Keycloak) → HIGH severity
- Industrial Control Systems (Siemens, Schneider, Rockwell) → CRITICAL severity
- Database engines (production-tagged devices) → HIGH severity
- Load balancers / reverse proxies → HIGH severity

### 2. Auto-Update Suppression
Lower noise for known auto-updating services:
- Chrome, Firefox version bumps → Suppress or INFO-only
- Node.js, Python patch versions → INFO-only
- Kubernetes components with auto-update enabled → INFO-only

### 3. Organizational Context
Use device tags/metadata for severity adjustment:
- Device tagged "production" → +1 severity level
- Device tagged "development" → -1 severity level
- Device in critical VLAN → +1 severity level

## Implementation Approach
- Extend notification catalog with severity adjustment rules
- Add service criticality mapping (similar to PORT_SEVERITY_MAP)
- Consider device metadata in severity calculation
- Make rules configurable per organization

## Architecture
```typescript
// packages/data-ops/src/notifications/catalog.ts
export const SERVICE_CRITICALITY_MAP: Record<string, SeverityAdjustment> = {
  'keycloak': { baseSeverity: 'HIGH', reason: 'Authentication gateway' },
  'siemens-plc': { baseSeverity: 'CRITICAL', reason: 'Industrial control' },
  'nginx': { baseSeverity: 'MEDIUM', autoUpdateSuppress: true },
};

function calculateDriftSeverity(
  driftType: 'product' | 'version' | 'name',
  service: ServiceInfo,
  deviceContext: DeviceContext
): NotificationSeverity {
  let baseSeverity = driftType === 'product' ? 'MEDIUM' : 'INFO';
  
  // Apply service criticality
  const criticalityRule = SERVICE_CRITICALITY_MAP[service.product];
  if (criticalityRule) {
    baseSeverity = criticalityRule.baseSeverity;
  }
  
  // Apply device context
  if (deviceContext.tags.includes('production')) {
    baseSeverity = increaseSeverity(baseSeverity);
  }
  
  return baseSeverity;
}
```

# Issue: Onboarding functions violate data-ops architecture

## Current Problem

Several functions in `apps/user-application/src/server/organization.ts` perform direct database operations, violating the data-ops architecture pattern.

**Affected Functions:**
- updateOrganizationOnboarding() - lines ~283-338
- completeOnboarding() - lines ~343-405
- getActiveOrganization() - lines ~410-465
- getOnboardingStatus() - lines ~470-605

These functions use raw database queries (db.select(), db.update(), eq(), and()) instead of calling data-ops query functions.

## Why This Matters

From CLAUDE.md architecture guide:
> "ALWAYS use data-ops queries, NEVER raw DB operations in apps"

**Benefits of moving to data-ops:**
1. Reusability - Functions can be used by other parts of the system
2. Testability - Business logic can be tested independently
3. Maintainability - Single source of truth for data operations
4. Consistency - All apps follow the same pattern

## What Should Be Done

### Step 1: Create Organization Onboarding Queries
File: packages/data-ops/src/queries/organizations.ts

Add new functions:
- updateOrganizationMetadata(organizationId, metadata)
- markOnboardingComplete(organizationId)
- getActiveOrganizationForUser(session)
- getOnboardingStatusForUser(userId, organizations)

### Step 2: Update Server Functions
File: apps/user-application/src/server/organization.ts

Refactor to call data-ops instead of raw DB operations.

### Step 3: Remove Direct DB Imports
After refactoring, remove these imports from organization.ts:
- import { getDb } from "@repo/data-ops/database/setup";
- import { organization, projects } from "@repo/data-ops/schema";
- import { and, eq } from "@repo/data-ops";

Server functions should only import from:
- @repo/data-ops (query functions)
- ./utils/auth (session helpers)
- @repo/logger (logging)

### Step 4: Export from Data-Ops
File: packages/data-ops/src/index.ts

Export new functions from organizations.ts

## Where to Look

title: Add automation hooks for SERVICE_DRIFT events (context sync, webhooks)
description:
Legacy daemon removed/re-added applications to business/technical contexts on drift. Implement modern equivalent via webhooks and automation hooks.

## Legacy Behavior (daemon.py)
When SERVICE_DRIFT detected:
1. Remove application from old context associations
2. Re-add application to contexts with new product/version
3. Trigger downstream workflows (asset reclassification, config checks)

## Proposed Implementation

### Core Feature: Webhook System
Allow users to configure webhooks that fire on SERVICE_DRIFT:

```json
POST /api/webhooks
{
  "url": "https://customer.com/drift-handler",
  "events": ["SERVICE_DRIFT"],
  "filters": {
    "severity": ["MEDIUM", "HIGH"],
    "ports": [22, 3389],  // Only SSH/RDP
    "productPatterns": ["OpenSSH.*", "nginx.*"]
  }
}
```

Webhook payload on drift:
```json
{
  "event": "SERVICE_DRIFT",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z",
  "device": {
    "id": "dev_123",
    "name": "web-server-01",
    "ip": "10.0.1.5"
  },
  "port": 80,
  "protocol": "tcp",
  "changes": {
    "product": { "old": "nginx", "new": "apache" },
    "version": { "old": "1.18.0", "new": "2.4.0" }
  },
  "severity": "MEDIUM",
  "notificationId": "notif_456",
  "scanRunId": "scan_789"
}
```

### Automation Hook System (Internal)
Allow plugins/extensions to register callbacks:

```typescript
// Example: Auto-reclassify on drift
registerDriftHook('auto-reclassify', async (drift) => {
  if (drift.changes.product.new === 'apache') {
    await updateDeviceTags(drift.device.id, ['web-server', 'apache']);
  }
});

// Example: Re-run compliance checks
registerDriftHook('compliance-check', async (drift) => {
  if (drift.severity === 'MEDIUM') {
    await queueComplianceScan(drift.device.id);
  }
});
```

### Built-in Automations (Optional)
- **Auto-tagging**: Apply tags based on product (e.g., nginx → "web-server")
- **Context sync**: Update project/asset groups when service changes
- **Alert routing**: Notify specific teams based on product (e.g., OpenSSH → security team)

## Implementation Tasks
- [ ] Design webhook schema (webhooks table)
- [ ] Implement webhook delivery system (retry, dead-letter queue)
- [ ] Add webhook management UI (create, edit, test, logs)
- [ ] Create automation hook registry (internal plugin system)
- [ ] Add built-in automations (auto-tagging, context sync)
- [ ] Document webhook payload schema and retry behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Users can configure webhooks for SERVICE_DRIFT events
- [ ] Webhook deliveries retried on failure (3x exponential backoff)
- [ ] Webhook logs show success/failure with payloads
- [ ] Internal hooks can register callbacks for drift events
- [ ] At least 1 built-in automation shipped (e.g., auto-tagging)

## Security Considerations
- Webhook URLs validated (no SSRF to internal IPs)
- Payload signed with HMAC (customer can verify authenticity)
- Rate limits on webhook deliveries per org

## Context
- Legacy: Context sync via Daemon.compare_parameters removed/added associations
- User pain: Manual reclassification after drift detected
- Related: sec-8sh (drift detection), sec-0lz (CVE re-enrichment)
- Similar to: GitHub webhooks, Stripe webhooks

title: Add service drift to scanRuns resultSummary
description:
Store detected service drift in scanRuns.resultSummary for historical tracking.

Schema addition to resultSummary:
{
  ...existing fields,
  serviceDrift?: {
    detected: boolean,
    changes: ServiceDriftResult[],  // From detectServiceDrift()
    baselineScanId: string,  // Which scan we compared against
    detectedAt: string  // ISO timestamp
  }
}

Integration:
- Call detectServiceDrift() in postback handler after persisting scan
- Get baseline scan (most recent successful scan before this one)
- If drift detected, add serviceDrift to resultSummary
- Update scanRuns record with modified resultSummary

Performance considerations:
- Drift detection should not block postback response
- Consider async processing (run in background after postback completes)
- Cache baseline scan to avoid repeated queries

Success criteria:
- Service drift persisted to database
- Historical drift queryable
- Performance acceptable (< 100ms overhead)
- No breaking changes to existing scans
